newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana-Malaysian shipyard gets giant client.
newsitem.headline: Ghana-Malaysian shipyard gets giant client.

text.p: Global Offshore International Ltd, a major world offshore construction company has decided to make Ghana's seaport of Tema its base for West Africa and to use its drydock to repair pipelaying barges.
"We already have a shed at the port. Currently we are negotiating the 10-year lease or our own berth where we can install a crane," Global Offshore's Captain Pete Acy told Reuters.
Global Offshore has two large barges operating off the West African coast.
On Tuesday, Acy moored his 7,800 tonne pipelaying barge "Global Cheyenne" at the PSC Tema Shipyard Ltd.
Earlier this year Global Offshore bought the 10,300 tonne pipelaying barge, DB21, from market leader Mc Dermott, renamed it "Global Comanche", and sailed it from Nigeria to Tema for refurbishing.
"We are getting ready to spend $5 million on refurbishment of the two barges," said Acy.
Part of the work will be done at the Tema 100,000 GRT dry dock, in which Penang Shipbuiding and Construction Ltd of Malaysia took a 60 percent stake last January.
With increased exploration and exploitation of oil and gas off West Africa's coast, Global Offshore expects "plenty of work" for its two barges, according to Acy.

The company is also eyeing the project of four West African states to build a 650 km offshore natural gas pipeline between Nigeria and Ghana. If Ghana agrees to import gas from Ivory Coast to fire a new power plant, a 200 km pipeline will have to be built from United Meridian's field off Ivory Coast to the plant at Takoradi.
Global Offshore recently built a 54 mile pipeline for United Meridian to bring its gas onshore in Ivory Coast, according to Acy.
